clue.text: Shut your mouth about hack being kept in the dark

indicators.note: the command to be quiet goes about, that is around, the newspaper word

parts.note: a rude order to be quiet, the same as 'hush up!'
a hack is a journalist, and the editor (ED) is the hack in charge

explanation.surface: Someone tells a journalist to keep quiet about a story that is being withheld from the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hushed up is suppressed and kept secret, so the public remain kept in the dark about it.

clue.text: Bottle rips out the inside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for courage, nerve
second meaning: the verb for disembowelling a fish or gutting a house

explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve, as in 'he lost his bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is the plural noun for courage and the verb for removing the entrails or interior of something.

clue.text: Lecherously give someone this prestigious organ!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give someone ... is to ogle them
second meaning: Private Eye's own jokey name for itself, an organ being a publication

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye often calls itself 'the Eye', and the self-praise of 'prestigious' is the magazine's running joke; 'organ' also hints at a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or magazine, and this is the familiar short name of the satirical fortnightly printing the puzzle.

clue.text: Contra picks up model after one

indicators.note: the getting and the model letter come after the article meaning one

parts.note: the indefinite article A means one
picks up in the sense of gains, acquires
the Ford Model T gives the letter T

explanation.surface: Reads like a Nicaraguan contra rebel acquiring a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin-derived for opposed to, the sense used in 'pros and contras'.

clue.text: Late royal's elevated, glorified state a cause for reproach?

indicators.note: in a down entry the princess's part is raised above the rest, so it sits first

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, known as Di, so Di's gives DIS
a state of grace is the blessed condition of the redeemed

explanation.surface: Suggests Diana's posthumous near-sainthood is itself something to be criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in 1997, around the national mourning for Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace is something shameful that brings blame or discredit on someone.

clue.text: Opportunity for all the electorate to vote — but obviously not for this party!

definitions.text: Opportunity for all the electorate to vote
definitions.meaning: a straight description of a popular vote on a single question

definitions.text: but obviously not for this party
definitions.meaning: the joke: a single-issue party named after such a vote stood in 1997 and almost nobody voted for it

explanation.surface: A national vote is offered, but nobody is going to vote for the party named after it.
explanation.walkthrough: James Goldsmith's Referendum Party, which wanted a vote on Europe, polled poorly at the 1997 general election.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebiscite on one question lets every voter in the country have a direct say.

clue.text: 'Two egos' Ross, transmogrified into a god!

indicators.note: transmogrified means changed in form, so the letters before it are rearranged into the god

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, so two of them give a pair of I's
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mocks the vanity of a broadcaster named Ross, so swollen-headed he becomes a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian deity of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Ineffectual type, but he's no plonker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: figuratively, a powerless or impotent person
second meaning: a castrated man; plonker is British slang for penis as well as for idiot

explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for a fool, which is the reading the surface wants, but it is also slang for the male member.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated man, and by extension anyone without power or influence, as in 'a political eunuch'.

clue.text: Old ready to get pisspoor Sun involved with age issues initially

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the Sun, the tabloid newspaper Private Eye routinely mocks as piss-poor

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Private Eye swipe at a tabloid's poor treatment of ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash, so old ready is old money. SUN, AGE and I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Guineas were old British gold coins worth 21 shillings, money from a former era.

clue.text: The systematic bad-mouthing of someone on the quiet?

definitions.meaning: an organised drive to spread damaging stories
both secretly and, literally, in hushed voices

explanation.definitionFit: A whispering campaign spreads rumours covertly in order to damage a person's reputation.

clue.text: A bit of a poseur — only has new money

indicators.note: only a piece of the following words is needed, the run of letters across them

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Sneers at a show-off whose only distinction is newly acquired wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New money' suggests the nouveau riche; in 1997 the single currency had not yet been launched.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro was the planned single European currency, brand new when this was set.

clue.text: Fergie, some geezer's beloved missus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sarah Ferguson's title as ... of York
second meaning: in cockney speech 'me old dutch(ess)' is a man's wife

explanation.walkthrough: Fergie is Sarah Ferguson, then the Duchess of York. 'My old Dutch', short for duchess, is a cockney term of affection for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a ducal title, and cockney slang for a man's wife.

clue.text: Minister's in terrible shit — pointless schism with Right

indicators.note: a terrible mess suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a point here is a compass point, and one of the S's is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A government minister finds himself in deep trouble over a split with the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Smith became Labour's Culture Secretary in 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a cabinet member in the first Blair government, so a named holder of ministerial office.

clue.text: Frottage is totally — well, somewhat — unfair to the elderly

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words, sitting across them

parts.note: the answer starts in the end of the first word and runs into the next two

explanation.surface: Suggests that rubbing against strangers is a pleasure the elderly are unfairly denied.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination on grounds of age, typically against older people.

clue.text: Our Dave's one for being self-denying

parts.note: Dave Spart is Private Eye's own long-running parody of a ranting leftist columnist
AN is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Praises the magazine's resident activist for his austere self-sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave Spart is a Private Eye character, hence 'our Dave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and frugal, after the harsh discipline of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: The two Davids' coming together — amorous carry-on without giving head

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is left off

parts.note: a dalliance is a light flirtation or affair

explanation.surface: Hints at a scandalous liaison between two men called David.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal–SDP Alliance of the 1980s was led by David Steel and David Owen; 'giving head' adds the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or partnership formed for mutual benefit, here a political pact.

clue.text: Finding, right, end's come off knob, get the beastly doctor round

indicators.note: the animal doctor goes round the other parts

parts.note: a doctor for beasts, an animal surgeon

indicators.note: the last letter of the slang word is lost

parts.note: knob is British slang for penis, as is dick

explanation.surface: A grim medical mishap: something has come off, and the vet is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the finding of a jury or court, its formal decision.

clue.text: See 10
Blokes loyal to old Labour leader who service Brenda?

definitions.note: describes the answer, a plural noun, by what they do

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Suggests Michael Foot's supporters are sexually servicing the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; 'loyal to' just links the men to the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Footmen are liveried male servants in a grand household, such as the royal one.

clue.text: Pass round Sun — sadly, it's representative of our country

indicators.note: the mountain pass goes around the reworked letters

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the word is in a sorry state, its letters shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tut at the Sun newspaper being regarded as the voice of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official appointed to represent a state's interests and citizens in a foreign city.

clue.text: Wilson, Heath feeling quite randy between them

indicators.note: the letters straddle the two names, so the answer lies between them

parts.note: the answer is the end of one prime minister's name joined to the start of the other's

explanation.surface: Imagines former prime ministers Harold Wilson and Edward Heath sharing a lustful moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on heat is the state of a female animal ready to mate, used jokingly of a lustful person.

clue.text: Best needs brief surgery to have flipping sex with the old woman!

parts.note: OP is the short form of operation

indicators.note: both a mild oath and a signal that the word for sex is turned over

parts.note: IT is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'
a familiar term for one's mother

explanation.surface: An outrageous boast about surgery followed by sex with one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum describes the most favourable or ideal condition or amount.

clue.text: Biood-sucker Brenda's heart

parts.note: a tick is a parasite that feeds on blood
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: Suggests the Queen is a parasite at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, from its ticking beat.

clue.text: Phoney mop cleaner — no shit!

indicators.note: the excrement is taken away from the hair wash

parts.note: a mop of hair is washed with shampoo
POO is a childish word for excrement

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a cleaning product is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mop' means a head of hair, not a floor mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake or pretence, and as an adjective means bogus or counterfeit.

clue.text: Relative to some, we hear, orgasm is a let-down

indicators.note: spoken in an accent, chiefly American, where the relative's title starts like 'pant'

parts.note: a father's or mother's sister, familiarly auntie
a sexual climax

explanation.surface: Remarks that sex is disappointing, at least for some relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing end to something that promised excitement.

clue.text: Flash (not Jack) is doubtful

indicators.note: the card abbreviation for Jack is excluded

parts.note: in a flash means in a jiffy, a moment

explanation.surface: Questions whether a man called Flash Jack is reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for uncertain or questionable.

clue.text: Old banger maybe gets some stick, but a boon for TV newsreaders

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old car, and AUTO is a car
a cue is a stick used in snooker and billiards

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car gets criticised, while newsreaders get help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets some stick' looks like criticism, but the stick is a snooker cue.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen device showing a presenter the script to read while facing the camera.

clue.text: A guy likely to engender a burning desire in us?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a guy is a stuffed figure of Guy Fawkes, a model of a person

definitions.text: likely to engender a burning desire in us?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a figure we want to set alight, as the British do on Bonfire Night

explanation.walkthrough: On 5 November the British burn a 'guy', a dummy of the Gunpowder Plotter Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: An effigy is a model of a person, especially one made to be burnt in protest or celebration.
